questions.stem: Which of the following is the molecular formula of an alkyne?
questions.explanation: Alkynes follow CnH2n-2, so for n = 3 the formula is C3H(6-2) = C3H4, which is propyne. The triple bond removes four hydrogen atoms relative to the corresponding alkane.

distractorRationale.a: C3H8 fits CnH2n+2 and is propane, an alkane
distractorRationale.b: C3H6 fits CnH2n and is propene, an alkene
distractorRationale.d: C3H7OH contains a hydroxyl group and is propanol, an alkanol

questions.stem: The reaction of ethene with hydrogen in the presence of a nickel catalyst is an example of
questions.explanation: The pi bond of the C=C opens and one hydrogen atom attaches to each carbon, giving C2H4 + H2 -> C2H6. Nothing is displaced and no small molecule is released, so this is an addition reaction. The same process hardens vegetable oil into margarine.

distractorRationale.a: Substitution replaces an atom already present and is characteristic of saturated alkanes
distractorRationale.c: Elimination removes a small molecule to create a double bond, the reverse of what happens here
distractorRationale.d: Condensation joins two molecules while expelling a small molecule such as water

questions.stem: A colourless gas rapidly decolourises orange bromine water at room temperature and in the dark. The gas is most likely
questions.explanation: Only unsaturated hydrocarbons decolourise bromine water in the dark, because bromine adds across the double bond to give colourless 1,2-dibromoethane. Alkanes can only react with bromine by substitution, and that requires ultraviolet light.

distractorRationale.a: Methane is saturated and leaves bromine water orange in the dark
distractorRationale.b: Ethane is likewise saturated and gives no reaction without ultraviolet light
distractorRationale.d: Carbon dioxide does not react with bromine water at all

questions.stem: The monomer used to manufacture poly(ethene) for water sachets and plastic bags is
questions.explanation: Addition polymerisation requires a monomer with a carbon-to-carbon double bond that can open and link to its neighbours. Ethene, CH2=CH2, does exactly this to form long (-CH2-CH2-)n chains with no other product.

distractorRationale.a: Ethane is saturated, so it has no double bond to open and cannot polymerise
distractorRationale.c: Ethanol contains a hydroxyl group and is not an addition monomer
distractorRationale.d: Ethyne is unsaturated but is used mainly as a welding fuel, not for making poly(ethene)

questions.stem: Ethyne is prepared in the laboratory by the action of water on
questions.explanation: Calcium carbide reacts vigorously with water to give ethyne and calcium hydroxide: CaC2 + 2H2O -> C2H2 + Ca(OH)2. The gas produced burns with a very hot flame, which is why it is used in oxy-acetylene welding.

distractorRationale.b: Calcium carbonate needs an acid, and it gives carbon dioxide rather than a hydrocarbon
distractorRationale.c: Calcium oxide reacts with water to give slaked lime only, with no gas evolved
distractorRationale.d: Aluminium carbide with water gives methane, not ethyne

questions.stem: Ethene reacts with steam at high temperature in the presence of a phosphoric acid catalyst. The organic product is
questions.explanation: Water adds across the double bond, with H attaching to one carbon and OH to the other: C2H4 + H2O -> C2H5OH. This catalytic hydration is the main industrial route to ethanol, faster and purer than fermentation though it relies on crude oil as a feedstock.

distractorRationale.a: Ethane would require the addition of hydrogen gas over a nickel catalyst
distractorRationale.c: Ethanoic acid needs a further oxidation step after the alcohol is formed
distractorRationale.d: That product comes from adding bromine, not steam
